<!-- Generated by make generate from the tests' doc comments; do not edit. -->

Every test below runs automatically; none is a manual check. The
descriptions come from the tests' own doc comments, so this page changes
with the tests.

A test passes when everything it checks holds. That is not always a run
that succeeds: several testcases make a run fail on purpose, and pass when
it fails in the way it should, with the right reason and nothing lost.
Their "Passes when" says so.

| How | What it runs | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `make test` | The unit and integration tests, with the race detector | Go; envtest's API server, which the target fetches |
| `make test-s3`, `make test-agent-s3` | TestS3 and TestS3Restart against a real bucket | The Vagrant test cluster's Garage |
| `make e2e` | The end-to-end testcases, after building and installing the images | The Vagrant test cluster |
| `make e2e-minio` | The same testcases against MinIO instead of Garage | The Vagrant test cluster |
| `make test-upgrade` | testcase18, an upgrade in the middle of a run | The Vagrant test cluster |
| `make test-crd`, `make test-chart`, `make test-templates` | The scripts under [Other tests](#other-tests) | A cluster for test-crd; podman or docker for test-templates |
| `make fuzz` | The Fuzz functions, for a while each | Go |

Each run of `make e2e` ends with a report, made by
{{< repolink "hack/report.sh" >}}, with every testcase's result, time and
output next to its description. The reports stay on the machine that ran
the tests, in `_out/reports/`. The [development page](/development/)
says how to set up the test cluster.

## End-to-end testcases

Each testcase runs a flow on the two-node test cluster with Talos, Garage as the storage and Zot as the registry, through the real controller, agents and components. The flows are in {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/" >}}, and most use the test component in {{< repolink "test/components/" >}}, whose sink checks every byte it reads.

### testcase01

Measures the system on the simplest flow: the time until every step runs, the latency of each chunk through two hops in object storage, and the throughput.

**Flow:** source → pass → sink, with BENCH_PASS_REPLICAS replicas of pass (default 1).

**What it tests:** that chunks go through the storage once and unchanged, and how fast (SPEC 13).

**Done to the run:** nothing.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded; sink, which checks every byte, has every chunk once and unchanged; and each step counted every chunk. The measurements go to the test report.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase01_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase01.yaml" >}}

### testcase02

Runs fan-out from one output to two steps, and fan-in to two ports of one step.

**Flow:** source → left (3 replicas) and right (2 replicas) → sink, with left and right on sink's two ports.

**What it tests:** that every consumer of an output gets every chunk (GO-36), that chunks are spread over the replicas by number (GO-76), and that a step with two inputs ends only when both have ended (GO-80, GO-95).

**Done to the run:** nothing.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded; sink has every chunk once on each port, unchanged; left's and right's replicas acked each chunk once, at replica n mod replicas; every stream has EOS and was consumed to its last chunk; and the counts are exact.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase02_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase02.yaml" >}}

### testcase03

Runs a step with ten replicas, where one gets chunks but writes none, and keeps the result in a bucket of its own.

**Flow:** source → filter (10 replicas) → sink. filter drops every chunk whose number is a multiple of its replica count, so replica 0 writes nothing.

**What it tests:** that a replica without output still ends its stream with EOS (GO-80); that chunks are spread over the replicas by number (GO-76); and that results go to spec.storage.resultsBucket, read with a Secret of their own (GO-129).

**Done to the run:** nothing.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded; sink has exactly the chunks that are not dropped, once and unchanged; replica 0 acked the multiples of 10, wrote none and has last 0; status.results names alpheus-results and alpheus-s3-results; nothing of the result is in the main bucket; and the counts are exact.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase03_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase03.yaml" >}}

### testcase04

Kills one step's pod halfway through its work, once for each step.

**Flow:** source → pass → sink, run three times.

**What it tests:** that each kind of step goes on correctly after a restart: a deterministic source goes on from the next chunk after checking the chunks it makes again (GO-92); pass goes on from the first unprocessed chunk and deletes output it never committed (GO-37, GO-70); and a stateful sink reads all its input again (GO-95, GO-100).

**Done to the run:** the first time source is killed when it has committed a quarter of its chunks; the second time pass when it has committed half its output; the third time sink when it has acked half its input, before EOS.

**Passes when:** each run is Succeeded with every chunk once and unchanged at sink, exact counts, one restart of the killed step, and no chunk objects left that were never committed.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase04_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase04.yaml" >}}

### testcase05

Runs a slow step and watches backpressure while the run goes.

**Flow:** source → slow (2 replicas) → sink, where slow waits before each chunk.

**What it tests:** that no consumer replica ever has more than maxUnacked chunks waiting that it has not acked (GO-35), and that the slowest replica sets the pace (GO-94).

**Done to the run:** nothing; the test samples source's manifest and slow's ack files while it runs.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded with every chunk once and exact counts; no sample shows a slow replica with more than maxUnacked chunks not acked; and the stream took at least chunks × delay / replicas.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase05_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase05.yaml" >}}

### testcase06

Kills random pods of a run with fan-out and fan-in until it is done (GO-56).

**Flow:** as testcase02: source → left (3) and right (2) → sink.

**What it tests:** that a run survives repeated crashes of any of its pods, wherever they happen.

**Done to the run:** a random pod is killed about every three seconds, BENCH_CHAOS_KILLS times (default 12) or until the run finishes. BENCH_CHAOS_SEED picks the pods, so a failure can be run again. The kills stop, so the run can finish: a stateful sink killed every few seconds would start over for ever.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded with every chunk once on each of sink's ports, unchanged; exact counts; the same checks of acks and streams as testcase02; and no chunk objects left that were never committed.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase06_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase06.yaml" >}}

### testcase07

Runs the Go and Python component templates in agent mode, the way users run them, and kills both.

**Flow:** source → go (templates/component-go, 2 replicas) → python (templates/component-python) → sink. Both templates have an empty match, so every chunk passes unchanged.

**What it tests:** that the templates work as real steps with the SDKs, and go on correctly after a restart (GO-37, GO-70).

**Done to the run:** go's replica 0 is killed when it has committed a quarter of its chunks, and python when it has committed half.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded with every chunk once and unchanged at sink; exact counters in both templates; one restart of each; and no chunk objects left that were never committed.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase07_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase07.yaml" >}}

### testcase08

Runs the flagship ETL flow of examples/meter-etl and checks that it is exact.

**Flow:** export → split → clean (4 replicas) → aggregate, with ETL_FILES files of ETL_ROWS rows (default 4 of 2,000,000), split into ETL_SPLIT_BYTES chunks (default 16 MiB).

**What it tests:** a realistic large-file ETL from end to end: every row generated is read once, bad rows are rejected and logged, and the totals are right (SPEC 13).

**Done to the run:** unless ETL_KILL=0, clean's replica 0 is killed when clean has read a quarter of the rows.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded; export, split and clean counted every row; clean rejected exactly the bad rows, kept the rest and logged an error for each, or counted it as dropped; the dataset has one chunk per split chunk; the totals per region and hour are the generator's; clean's replica 0 restarted once if it was killed; and no chunk objects are left that were never committed. The measurements go to the test report, and the results are deleted at the end, since the dataset is large.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase08_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase08.yaml" >}}

### testcase09

Takes the storage away in the middle of a run, once for 20 seconds and once for 3 minutes.

**Flow:** source → pass → sink, run twice.

**What it tests:** that the agents wait for the storage with backoff instead of failing (GO-136).

**Done to the run:** the storage (Garage, or MinIO with ALPHEUS_E2E_STORAGE=minio) is scaled to 0 in the middle of the stream and back up after 20 seconds, and in the second run after 3 minutes.

**Passes when:** each run is Succeeded with every chunk once and unchanged, exact counts and no restarts at all.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase09_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase09.yaml" >}}

### testcase10

Deletes the controller's pod twice in the middle of a run.

**Flow:** as testcase02: source → left (3) and right (2) → sink.

**What it tests:** that a running run needs neither the controller nor its signal hub: the agents poll the manifests (GO-40), and the new controller takes over the run.

**Done to the run:** the controller's pod, with the signal hub in it, is deleted when sink has read a quarter of its input, and again at three quarters.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded with every chunk once, exact counts and no restarts, and its status never went backwards.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase10_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase10.yaml" >}}

### testcase11

Gives a run keys the storage refuses: the right key ID with a wrong secret.

**Flow:** source → sink.

**What it tests:** that refused keys fail the run at once instead of being retried as an outage (GO-137), with a reason a program can rely on (GO-138).

**Done to the run:** nothing; the run's storage Secret has the wrong secret.

**Passes when:** the run is Failed within two minutes, with a message that the storage refused the keys and the reason for it; no step restarted; no pods are left; and deleting the run does not hang on data the keys cannot delete. The run is expected to fail: the test passes when it fails this way.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase11_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase11.yaml" >}}

### testcase12

Runs out of space in the middle of a run: the bucket has a quota of 20 MiB, far less than the run needs.

**Flow:** source → sink.

**What it tests:** that a full bucket fails the run instead of being waited for as an outage (GO-136), that a restart is not tried, since it would find the bucket just as full (GO-77), and that what was committed still holds (GO-115).

**Done to the run:** nothing; the bucket's quota is reached during the stream. Garage refuses the first write over the quota, so source fails. MinIO counts a bucket's usage now and then, so it lets writes through until it has counted them, and then refuses one in whichever step writes next.

**Passes when:** the run is Failed, with a reason that says the bucket is full and not that the storage is unreachable; on Garage it failed in source; the manifest has some but not all of the chunks; no step restarted; every chunk the manifests list exists and is unchanged; and source's counters match its manifest. The run is expected to fail: the test passes when it fails this way.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase12_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase12.yaml" >}}

### testcase13

Gives sink chunks larger than its scratch space: 1 MiB of scratch and chunks of 4 MiB.

**Flow:** source → sink.

**What it tests:** that the agent refuses a chunk that does not fit, with an error that names the scratch folder, before the folder fills up and Kubernetes evicts the pod (GO-106, GO-138).

**Done to the run:** nothing; the step's scratch size is too small.

**Passes when:** the run is Failed because a chunk does not fit in the scratch folder, with the reason in sink; sink failed after its one restart; and no pod was evicted. The run is expected to fail: the test passes when it fails this way.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase13_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase13.yaml" >}}

### testcase14

Runs a component with a bug and checks everything a person or a tool needs to find it.

**Flow:** source → pass → sink, where pass panics on a chunk.

**What it tests:** the reason as a code and in the component's words (GO-138, GO-139); the Kubernetes events and the Ready condition (GO-139); the kept logs of both attempts and the failed attempt's inputs (GO-140); the agent's live metrics (GO-51); and alpheus replay of the last attempt on its own, on the chunks it had open, at debug level (GO-141).

**Done to the run:** nothing; the bug fails pass on both of its attempts.

**Passes when:** the run is Failed with the reason ComponentFailed in pass replica 0, and a message with what the component said; the events and the Ready condition say the same; the logs and the failure of both attempts are kept; sink's agent served its metrics; and the replay exits with code 1 and logs the same panic at debug level. The run is expected to fail: the test passes when it fails this way.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase14_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase14.yaml" >}}

### testcase15

Looks at a failed run through alpheus ui in the cluster, installed by the chart and reached through a port-forward, as the chart's notes say (GO-143).

**Flow:** source → pass → sink, where pass fails as in testcase14.

**What it tests:** that the page in the cluster shows the runs of every namespace, a failed replica's attempts, kept logs and failure, and that its replay button runs the attempt as a pod in the run's namespace (GO-141).

**Done to the run:** nothing; the bug fails the run.

**Passes when:** the run is Failed with ComponentFailed; the page lists it among the runs of every namespace; it shows the attempts and the kept log; and the replay runs in the cluster, fails the same way at debug level, and its pod is deleted afterwards.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase15_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase15.yaml" >}}

### testcase16

Runs a flow across two nodes, with the steps placed by nodeSelector (GO-144).

**Flow:** source → pass (2 replicas) → sink, with pass on the worker and the others on the control plane.

**What it tests:** that a step's nodeSelector places its pods, and that chunks go between nodes through the storage.

**Done to the run:** nothing.

**Passes when:** both nodes are Ready; the run is Succeeded with every chunk once, unchanged and exact counts; and each pod ran on the node its step asks for.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase16_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase16.yaml" >}}

### testcase17

Loses a node in the middle of a run (GO-67).

**Flow:** source → pass → sink, with pass on the worker.

**What it tests:** that a run survives a dead machine: the replica on the lost node gets a new attempt elsewhere, (GO-67).

**Done to the run:** the worker is powered off and its Node deleted, as a cloud provider does with a dead machine, and powered on again afterwards. It needs virsh and the worker's VM in ALPHEUS_E2E_WORKER_VM, which hack/e2e.sh sets.

**Passes when:** the run is Succeeded with every chunk once and exact counts; pass restarted once, with its new attempt on the control plane; and the worker is Ready again within 10 minutes.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase17_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase17.yaml" >}}

### testcase18

Upgrades the chart in the middle of a run (GO-66).

**Flow:** source → pass (2 replicas) → sink, with an older commit's test component, since a user's components are not rebuilt when Alpheus is upgraded.

**What it tests:** that a run started under an older controller and agent finishes under this commit's controller; that new attempts keep the agent the run started with (GO-24, GO-164); and that a run started after the upgrade gets this commit's agent.

**Done to the run:** when sink has read a quarter of its first stream, the chart, CRD, controller and agent are upgraded; then a pass replica, and later the stateful sink, are deleted.

**Passes when:** every pod ran the old agent before the upgrade; the run is Succeeded with every chunk once and exact counts; pass and sink restarted once, their new attempts with the old agent; status.agentImage is the old agent; the status never went backwards; and a run started afterwards runs this commit's agent.

It runs only with make test-upgrade (hack/test-upgrade.sh), which installs the older commit first and sets:

```
ALPHEUS_E2E_UPGRADE             the command that upgrades to this
                            commit's chart and images
ALPHEUS_E2E_UPGRADE_BENCH_IMAGE the older commit's test component
ALPHEUS_E2E_UPGRADE_AGENT_IMAGE the older commit's agent
```

and AGENT_IMAGE is this commit's agent. make e2e skips it.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase18_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase18.yaml" >}}

### testcase19

Sets a bad chunk aside instead of failing the run, with failurePolicy continue (GO-97), as docs/dead-letters.md describes.

**Flow:** source → pass (2 replicas, failurePolicy continue), where pass has testcase14's bug and fails on source's chunk 5, which is replica 1's. pass's output is the result.

**What it tests:** that a replica that gives up stops alone while the others go on; that the run ends PartiallySucceeded; that the chunk it failed on and every chunk it did not process are kept for alpheus replay --skipped.

**Done to the run:** nothing; the bug fails replica 1 on both of its attempts.

**Passes when:** the run is PartiallySucceeded with the reason FailedReplicas; replica 0 succeeded and replica 1 failed with ComponentFailed after one restart; every chunk of source is in the result once or counted in failedChunks, and chunk 5 is not in the result; both results have ended; and alpheus replay --skipped fetches exactly replica 1's unprocessed chunks, starting with chunk 5. The run is expected to succeed only partly: the test passes when it ends this way.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase19_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase19.yaml" >}}

### testcase20

Checks what a run's pods can reach: its NetworkPolicy and ServiceAccount (SPEC 6.1, step 2).

**Flow:** source → sink, run twice. source tries the Kubernetes API, Garage's admin port and Zot before it writes, and counts what it reached.

**What it tests:** that a run's policy blocks everything but the storage and the signal hub, that its ServiceAccount has no token, and that a policy of the user's own adds to it, as docs/isolation.md shows.

**Done to the run:** before the second run, the test adds a policy that lets source reach Zot.

**Passes when:** both runs are Succeeded; in the first, all three were blocked; in the second, Zot was reached and the other two blocked; and the run owns its NetworkPolicy and ServiceAccount, which does not mount a token. It needs a network plugin that enforces NetworkPolicies; hack/e2e.sh sets ALPHEUS_E2E_NETWORK_POLICY=0 on a cluster with flannel.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase20_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase20.yaml" >}}

### testcase21

Runs the debug example of docs/debug-example.md, and gets its results and error log out with the CLI.

**Flow:** orders → filter (3 replicas) → merge → sort, with customers as a side input to merge.

**What it tests:** that each new attempt gets the side input again (GO-167); that a failed attempt is kept with all of its side input (GO-140); that a step's log level can be set (GO-166); and alpheus results get, ls, cat and copy and alpheus errors, which find the storage by the annotations on its Secret (GO-147 to GO-156).

**Done to the run:** nothing; version 1 of merge has a bug. Then the run is created again with version 2 of merge at debug level.

**Passes when:** with version 1 the run is Failed in merge, after three attempts that all panic the same way, without logging a single error, and the failure is kept with the side input; with version 2 the run is Succeeded, merge joined every order filter passed and warned about each blank region; results get of the failed run with --complete exits 1, saying the results are incomplete; results get of version 2 fetches every chunk with its size; results ls and cat agree with it; results copy is done by the storage and finds every copy there when run again; and alpheus errors lists one entry per warning.

Source: {{< repolink "test/e2e/testcase21_test.go" >}}, flow {{< repolink "test/e2e/testdata/testcase21.yaml" >}}

## Unit and integration tests

These run with `make test`, without a cluster. The controller's tests run against a real API server (envtest), and the agent's run whole flows in one process against an in-memory store.

### cmd/alpheus-agent

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestHealthAndReady` | The agent answers /healthz while it runs, and /readyz once it serves the component's socket (GO-52). |

### cmd/alpheus-controller

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestNetworkOptions` | Checks that the controller's network flags become its options: the signal hub's port, the storage's ports and the policy's egress rules, no NetworkPolicy when it is off, and an error for a bad port or bad JSON. |

### examples/debug-session/merge

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestMergeV1FailsOnBlankRegion` | Version 1 fails on the first order from a customer without a region, on day 7, with exit code 1 and where it panicked. |

### examples/debug-session/merge-v2

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestMergeV2HandlesBlankRegion` | Version 2 joins every order, writes None for a blank region, and warns about each with the code blank_region. |

### examples/meter-etl/meter

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestParse` | Checks that a meter reading is parsed, and that each kind of bad row is rejected with its own error: too few columns, a bad meter ID, no region, a bad timestamp, a missing, negative or too precise value. |
| `TestFlow` | Runs the four steps in local mode, clean as two replicas, and checks the totals, the counters and the dataset against Expected. |

### hack/changelog

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestCheck` | Accepts a well-formed changelog and refuses one without an Unreleased section first, with a release that lacks a part or has them out of order, with a version twice, or with a heading that is neither. |
| `TestNotes` | Gives a release's section, with or without the v, and fails with a message for a version the changelog has no section for, so hack/release.sh stops there. |
| `TestDocs` | Makes docs/changes.md: front matter instead of the title, and the Unreleased section, and only that, inside the planned shortcode and marked as not released yet. |
| `TestChangelog` | Checks the repository's own CHANGELOG.md, as make ci does. |

### hack/testreport

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestParse` | Checks that the test report reads go test -json output right: passed, failed, skipped and unfinished tests, their time, and the package's own output. |
| `TestRender` | Checks that the report page shows a failed run with its subtests, escaped output and metadata, and that a report ID that could leave the folder is refused. |
| `TestDocs` | Checks that the report takes each test's description from its doc comment and splits it into paragraphs and code blocks. |

### internal/agent

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestPipelineWithHub` | Runs generate → filter (10 replicas) → sum through the agents, with the signal hub, on 30 chunks: every chunk arrives once, unchanged, and the sum is right. |
| `TestFanOutFanIn` | Runs generate → left (3 replicas) and right (2 replicas) → sum, with right on a port of its own: every chunk reaches each consuming step once through its own ack files (GO-36), and sum gets EOS only when both inputs have ended. |
| `TestPipelinePollingOnly` | Without signals the agents find everything by polling (GO-40). |
| `TestSourceRestart` | A restarted source must close the same chunks again; they are compared and discarded (GO-92). |
| `TestRestartFilter` | Crashes a filter replica after three chunks and runs every replica again as a new attempt: the result must be as if nothing happened (GO-37, GO-70, GO-74). |
| `TestRestartStatefulSum` | sum keeps its state in memory only, so after a crash every chunk is read again and the sum is still right (GO-95, GO-100). |
| `TestRestartAfterStatefulEnded` | A stateful step restarted after it committed and ended its output, as when its pod dies between that write and the end of the pod, has nothing left to do: its OnEOS must not run on an empty state, which would make a careful component fail on every restart (GO-95; found by testcase06). |
| `TestFencing` | An agent stops when a newer attempt owns its stream (GO-68). |
| `TestBackpressure` | Backpressure: with nobody consuming, a producer stops after maxUnacked chunks per consumer replica (GO-35). |
| `TestManyChunksPerInput` | A step may make more chunks from one input chunk than maxUnacked: its output is not committed until the input chunk is done, so the consumer cannot ack it before, and backpressure must not wait for that (GO-35). Here filter writes each DK line five times, each in its own chunk: ten chunks per input chunk, with maxUnacked 2. |
| `TestBackpressureClosedReplica` | A consumer replica whose ack file the controller closed, after it failed for good with failurePolicy continue, no longer holds the producer back (GO-35, GO-97). With maxUnacked 2 and nobody consuming, replica 0 stops generate at chunk 5, which it could not before, and replica 1 is closed. |
| `TestAckFencing` | An agent whose ack file has a newer epoch, or was closed by the controller, stops instead of writing it (GO-68, GO-97). |
| `TestCrashAtEveryWrite` | Stops the whole pipeline at each write the agents make in turn, then runs every replica again as a new attempt. Whichever commit step it stopped between (SPEC 7.3 and 7.4), the result must have nothing missing and nothing twice (GO-74): the sum is right, every chunk is acked once, and the counters and the error log are exact (GO-115, GO-118). |
| `TestMetrics` | The agent's metrics carry the run, step and replica, and skip what is not a count (GO-51, GO-116). |
| `TestReason` | The agent fails with a reason code for each kind of error (GO-138). |
| `TestS3Pipeline` | Runs testcase03's shape against a real bucket, with signals through the hub and a restart of the stateful step, for example against Garage in the Vagrant cluster: `make test-agent-s3` |
| `TestS3Restart` | Runs the pipeline against a real bucket, crashes the sum after five chunks, and runs it again as a new attempt: the result must be as if nothing happened. It runs with make test-s3, and is skipped without ALPHEUS_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT. |
| `TestSideInputToEveryReplica` | Every replica of the consumer gets every chunk of a side input, not its share of them. |
| `TestSideInputAfterRestart` | A new attempt gets the side input again and builds its lookup data anew, while the main input goes on from the first chunk not committed. With one replica it is the restart alone that is tested. |
| `TestSideInputHasNoOutput` | A side input chunk can have no output of its own: a new attempt reads it again, so the output would be written twice. |

### internal/chunk

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestAcks` | Checks an ack file: acks in order, a repeated ack ignored, an ack out of order refused, and the file's format and round trip. |
| `TestParseAcksRejects` | Checks that an ack file with another version, acks out of order, chunk 0, a repeated ack or impossible observed totals is refused. |
| `TestAcksTestcase03Check` | The check testcase03 makes on the filter replicas' ack files (GO-84): disjoint, together exactly 1-100, chunk n at replica n mod 10. |
| `TestChecksumRoundTrip` | Checks that a chunk written with its size and SHA-256 reads back unchanged through the verifying reader. |
| `TestChecksumDetectsCorruption` | Checks that a chunk with a changed byte, a missing byte or an extra byte fails with ErrChecksum. |
| `FuzzParseManifest` | Feeds the manifest parser cut-off, foreign and hand-changed files (GO-58): it never panics, and a manifest it accepts marshals to the same bytes again and can be appended to and ended. |
| `FuzzParseSegment` | Does the same for sealed segments: one that is accepted has exactly 1,000 chunks in order and marshals to the same bytes again. |
| `FuzzParseAcks` | Does the same for ack files: one that is accepted marshals to the same bytes again, knows every chunk it acked, and takes the next ack. |
| `TestManifestAppend` | Checks that chunks are added to a manifest in order from 1, and that a gap or a chunk added twice is refused. |
| `TestManifestSealsSegments` | Checks that every 1,000 chunks are sealed into a segment with the right name and numbers, and that the count includes them (GO-32). |
| `TestManifestEndsEmpty` | A replica that drops every chunk it gets ends its stream with no chunks and eos (GO-80, testcase03). |
| `TestManifestConsumedNeverMovesBack` | Checks that how far an input stream is consumed never goes back (SPEC 7.4). |
| `TestManifestCheckEpoch` | Checks that a manifest from an older attempt and one from a newer attempt are told apart from the reader's own (GO-68). |
| `TestManifestRoundTrip` | Checks that a manifest with counters, a source chunk and a consumed stream is written and read back unchanged. |
| `TestParseManifestRejects` | Checks that a manifest from a newer version, with unknown fields or trailing data, epoch 0, EOS without its last chunk, a gap, a short checksum or a bad extension is refused, so a file is never half understood. |
| `TestEdgeName` | Checks edge names: &lt;from&gt;-&lt;to&gt;, with the output only when it is not the default one. |
| `TestStreamKeys` | Checks the object keys of a stream: its prefix, chunks, manifest, segments and ack files, and the prefix of a result. |
| `TestAssignPartitions` | Every chunk goes to exactly one replica, the same one each time. |
| `TestAssignTestcase03` | testcase03 relies on replica 0 getting exactly the chunks filter drops: 10, 20 ... 100 (SPEC 12.1). |
| `TestAssignSpreadsProducers` | With many producer replicas that each make a few chunks, the producer's number spreads the work instead of loading the first replicas (GO-76). |
| `TestAssignOneReplica` | Checks that a step with one replica, or none given, gets every chunk on replica 0. |
| `TestValidExt` | Checks which file extensions a chunk may have: lower-case letters and digits, one part, at most 16 characters. |

### internal/cli

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestRunOverrides` | run can give a step another image and log level, and the run another name, without editing the flow file (GO-161, GO-166). |
| `TestRunGetCancel` | Checks run, get and cancel: a run is created once, get lists it as text, JSON and YAML and shows the status the controller writes, and cancel sets spec.cancel. |
| `TestValidate` | Checks that validate accepts a good flow without creating it, rejects bad flows with exit code 1 and a reason, warns about an image without a digest with --local, and wants -f. |
| `TestWatch` | Checks that watch prints each change of the status, one JSON object per line, until the run finishes, and exits with 1 when the run failed. |
| `TestChunks` | Checks that chunks shows an edge's manifests as text and JSON, and names the run's edges when asked for one it does not have. |
| `TestResultsGC` | Checks that results gc lists what it would delete with --dry-run, asks before deleting, deletes only results whose resultsTTL has run out, keeps results whose run is gone unless --orphans, and wants its flags. |
| `TestLogs` | Checks that logs shows every step's log or one step's, as text or JSON, and says so for a run without pods, a missing step or a container that is not there. |
| `TestVersion` | Checks that version shows the CLI's, the controller's and the CRD's versions, and the CLI's own when there is no cluster. |
| `TestReference` | The website's CLI reference has every command and its own flags, and leaves out the flags every command has. |
| `TestReplayAndKeptLogs` | replay fetches a failed attempt's inputs, checked, and runs the same image on them in local mode at debug level (GO-141); logs --kept shows the attempt's logs (GO-140). |
| `TestUI` | The ui answers only on localhost, serves the runs, a replica's kept logs and failures, and runs replay only with the page's token (GO-142). |
| `TestReplayInCluster` | replay --with cluster runs the attempt as a pod in the run's namespace: the agent's image fetches the inputs, the step's image runs on them at debug level, the logs are printed and the pod is deleted (GO-141, GO-143). |
| `TestUIInCluster` | In the cluster the ui shows every namespace, answers to the host names it is given, and can have replay off (GO-143). |
| `TestUIHelpIsTheGuide` | The page's help is docs/ui.md, the guide on the website, copied by make generate; the page renders it at #/help. |
| `TestFailedReplica` | replay takes the replica that stopped the run, else one that gave up or failed, so the command alpheus get shows works without --replica. |
| `TestResultsGetCatLs` | results get, cat and ls read only the committed chunks, check them, and put them where SPEC 9.1 says (GO-147, GO-151, GO-153). |
| `TestResultsGetFolder` | results get writes only into an empty folder or the same run's, and --force writes only the run's own files (GO-148). |
| `TestResultsGetResume` | A fetch that was stopped goes on from its .partial, only from the same version of the object; a chunk that does not match its manifest is an error and leaves nothing (GO-149). |
| `TestResultsIncomplete` | A replica without EOS is fetched and said to be incomplete; --complete makes that an error (GO-152). |
| `TestErrors` | errors shows the committed error log, counts it per code, and saves it (GO-154). |
| `TestStorageAddress` | The storage's address is found in the order GO-156 gives, and an error says which address was tried and what to set. |
| `TestNext` | A finished run's status ends with the commands that fit it (GO-146). |
| `TestResultsGetSpace` | results get checks the free space before it fetches, and asks before more than 10 GiB (GO-150). The sizes come from the manifest, so the chunks need not exist. |
| `TestResultsCopy` | results copy copies the committed chunks and the index to another bucket, checks what it streams, goes on where it stopped, and keeps to an empty prefix or the run's own (GO-155). |

### internal/controller

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestPodsAndSuccess` | Runs a flow through the controller and checks each step's pod: the agent as a native sidecar with the configured image, the agent's and the component's settings, no secrets for the component, the log level, a writable /tmp on a read-only root, a certificate per attempt (GO-41), and the run Succeeded when every pod has. |
| `TestFailureReason` | A pod's failure names the agent's reason when the agent failed, such as storage that stayed unreachable (GO-136), with a reason code a program can rely on (GO-138), and what the component left in its termination message (GO-139). |
| `TestRestartsThenStop` | A failed attempt gets a new pod; when the restarts are used up the run stops (GO-67, GO-77). |
| `TestFailurePolicyContinue` | With failurePolicy continue a failed replica's streams are closed with a higher epoch, and the run ends PartiallySucceeded (GO-97). |
| `TestStorageFullStops` | A full bucket stops the run at the first failed attempt, without the restarts it has left and also with failurePolicy continue: a new attempt would only find the bucket full again. |
| `TestSideInput` | A side input goes to every replica's agent as one, a failed attempt keeps all of it for a replay next to the chunks it had not finished, and a side input's chunks count as acked when every replica has read them (GO-167). |
| `TestLogLevel` | A step's logLevel reaches its component as ALPHEUS_LOG_LEVEL, and only that step's (GO-166); the CRD refuses another level. |
| `TestInvalidRuns` | Checks that a run with a cycle or an image without a digest fails with a message and no pods, and that the API server rejects a step that reads its own output (GO-23). |
| `TestStorageTimeout` | spec.storage.timeout is checked by the API server and immutable like the rest of storage, compared as a duration, so a client that reads "10m" and writes it back as "10m0s" changes nothing (GO-136). |
| `TestCancel` | Checks that spec.cancel stops a run: it is Cancelled, its pods go, and steps and replicas that had not finished are Stopped, not left Running or Pending. |
| `TestFinalizer` | Deleting a run deletes runs/&lt;uid&gt;/ but keeps its results (GO-20, GO-78). Deleting a namespace deletes the storage Secret and the run together. The run's finalizer on the Secret keeps the keys until runs/&lt;uid&gt;/ is deleted; then both go, and the result stays (GO-20, GO-78). |
| `TestRefusedKeys` | Keys the storage refuses fail the run at once, with no restarts, and the run can still be deleted, leaving its data (GO-137). |
| `TestFinalizerWithoutSecret` | A run whose storage Secret never existed is still deleted, leaving its data, instead of hanging. |
| `TestStatusFromStorage` | Status shows edges, results and counters from storage (GO-79, GO-115). |
| `TestHubMTLS` | The hub accepts an agent with a certificate for the current attempt of a replica of the run it uses, and turns away a client without a certificate, an older attempt, another run and a certificate that names no agent (GO-41). |
| `TestLoadCACreates` | The first LoadCA in a namespace creates the CA and returns it; the next one reads the same CA back. |
| `TestSpecNotRewritten` | Adding the finalizer must not write the spec back as Go encodes it: resultsTTL stays 168h, not 168h0m0s. |
| `TestResultsBucket` | With a results bucket, the agents write results there, and status.results names that bucket and the Secret that can only read it, never the agents' key (GO-129). |
| `TestAgentImagePinned` | A run keeps the agent it started with: a new attempt after the controller has another agent still gets the run's (GO-24, GO-164). |
| `TestRunAgent` | A run from before status.agentImage keeps the agent its oldest pod runs; one without pods gets the controller's (GO-164). |
| `TestSealedTotals` | A result's bytes and counters include the chunks in sealed segments, not only those still in manifest.json (GO-32). |
| `TestScheduling` | A step's nodeSelector, tolerations and affinity go to its pods (GO-144). |
| `TestRunObjects` | A run gets a ServiceAccount with no token and a NetworkPolicy, both its own, and its pods use them (SPEC 6.1, step 2). A policy that is changed is put right, and one that is deleted comes back. |
| `TestRunObjectsNotOurs` | A ServiceAccount with the run's name that is not the run's own stops the run before any pod starts. |
| `TestNetworkPolicy` | The policy's storage rule follows the endpoint, or the ports and peers the installation gives; without a hub there is no rule for it, and the agent's metrics port is the only way in. |
| `TestStatusLimit` | A run's status is written at most once a second; other runs are not held back by it (GO-22). |

### internal/replay

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestParse` | Checks that a failure.json is read, and that one whose ports or files could climb out of the replay folder, or with impossible chunks, sizes or checksums, is refused. |
| `FuzzParse` | Checks that a failure record from the bucket can never make Fetch write outside the replay folder (GO-58, GO-141). |
| `TestFetchWritesIndex` | Fetch writes the index that gives each fetched chunk its producer and number in local mode. |

### internal/signal/builtin

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestForwardsPerEdge` | Checks that the signal hub forwards a ready signal only to those who subscribed to its edge. |
| `TestReconnects` | A client that loses the hub reconnects and subscribes again. |

### internal/store

| Test | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `TestIdentify` | Identify knows the tested stores by what they answer a request without keys, and no other (GO-69). |
| `TestTransient` | Checks which storage errors are waited out: a refused or reset connection, a cut-off body and 5xx and 429 answers, but not refused keys, a missing object, a changed object or a cancel (GO-136). |
| `TestRefused` | Checks which storage errors mean the keys or the bucket are refused, so the run fails at once (GO-137). |
| `TestRetryUntilBack` | Checks that a call is retried until the storage answers. |
| `TestRetryGivesUp` | Checks that retrying stops after the timeout with ErrUnreachable and the last error. |
| `TestRetryNotPermanentErrors` | Checks that a refused request is not retried, and that timeout 0 tries once. |
| `TestRetryStopsOnCancel` | Checks that retrying stops when the context is cancelled. |
| `TestResumingReader` | Checks that a download broken off goes on where it stopped, with the same version of the object. |
| `TestResumingReaderSameVersionOnly` | Checks that a download is not continued from an object that was overwritten in between, so two versions are never mixed. |
| `TestResumingReaderWithoutTimeout` | Checks that without a timeout a broken download fails with its own error. |
| `TestWithResults` | Keys under results/ go to the results store, every other key to the main store, and a listing across both stays in lexical order (GO-129). |
| `TestMemory` | Runs the store checks against the in-memory store the other tests use: a missing object, put, overwrite and get, unknown size, a chunk with its checksum, list and delete a prefix, size, and a ranged read of the same version. |
| `TestS3` | Runs the same checks against a real bucket when ALPHEUS_TEST_S3_\* is set, for example against Garage in the Vagrant cluster: `make test-s3` |
| `TestNewS3RejectsBadEndpoints` | Checks that an endpoint without http:// or https://, with another scheme or with a path is refused. |
